title: Physics in communication
competency: Explain wired and wireless communication in terms of physics.

keywords.def: Sending messages with electromagnetic waves, without a wire.
A thin glass fibre that carries light signals.

en.text: Communication sends a message from one point to another through a medium. Wired systems use metal wire or optical fibre. Wireless systems use radio waves, microwaves and infrared, which travel through air and even empty space at the speed of light. A transmitter puts the message on a wave; a receiver picks it up.

screens.title: No wires
screens.ask: Your phone talks to a tower kilometres away with no wire. What carries the message?
screens.after:
Radio waves and microwaves carry the message.
They are electromagnetic waves, so they need no wire and no medium.
They travel at the speed of light, even through space.

screens.title: Physics in communication
paras: Communication is transferring a message from one point to another.
Wired systems use wire and optical fibre.
Wireless systems use radio waves, microwaves and infrared.
Electromagnetic theory, circuits, electronics and wave behaviour are all needed.

screens.title: Radio wavelength
screens.ask: Change the frequency. The speed stays c. Watch the wavelength.
screens.note: FM radio ≈ 100 MHz: λ ≈ 3 m. Mobile phones ≈ 900 MHz: λ ≈ 0.33 m.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Sending messages with electromagnetic waves, without a wire.
A thin glass fibre that carries light signals.

screens.text: Wired or wireless: which is a wired communication system?
screens.why:
A wired system sends the signal along a cable.
An optical fibre is a glass cable that carries light.
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and satellite phones use waves through the air.
Answer: optical fibre.

screens.text: Wireless communication works because electromagnetic waves
screens.why:
Sound needs air or another medium.
Electromagnetic waves need no medium at all.
They even cross empty space, as from a satellite.
Answer: they need no medium to travel.

screens.text: Wireless media, true or false: a TV remote control uses infrared.
screens.why:
The book lists radio waves, microwaves and infrared as wireless media.
A TV remote sends pulses of infrared light.
So the statement is true.

screens.text: Speed of radio waves: mobile network radio waves travel at about
screens.why:
Radio waves are electromagnetic waves.
All electromagnetic waves travel at c ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s in air.
Trap: 340 m/s is the speed of sound, not radio.
Trap: 3 × 10⁵ is c in km/s, not m/s.

screens.ask: Satellite signal delay: a signal goes up to a satellite 36 000 km high and back down. At 3 × 10⁵ km/s this takes ___ s
screens.why:
Path: up and down = 2 × 36 000 km = 72 000 km.
Formula: t = d/c.
Substitute: t = 72 000 km ÷ 300 000 km/s.
Result: t = 0.24 s.
Trap: one way only gives 0.12 s.
screens.clue: Up and down: double the height.

items.text: Brainstorming question 1.16: which technologies are wireless? Pick all that apply.
items.why:
A mobile phone uses radio waves to the tower.
Wi-Fi uses radio waves (microwaves) in the home.
Bluetooth uses short-range radio waves.
A landline telephone uses a wire, so it is wired.

test.why:
Wireless means no cable.
The signal is carried by electromagnetic waves.
The book lists radio waves, microwaves and infrared.

test.text: Wired media: an optical fibre carries
test.why:
An optical fibre is a thin glass thread.
Light signals travel along it by total internal reflection.
Answer: light.

test.text: How communication works, true or false: communication needs a medium of transmission.
test.why:
A message must be carried from sender to receiver.
The book calls the carrier the medium of transmission.
It can be a wire, a fibre, or waves through air or space.
So the statement is true.

test.text: Physics for wireless: which knowledge is essential for wireless communication?
test.why:
Wireless signals are electromagnetic waves.
To make, send and receive them you need electromagnetic theory.
Fluid mechanics and geology do not carry signals.

test.ask: Signal travel time: a radio signal crosses 600 km at 3 × 10⁵ km/s in ___ s
test.why:
Formula: t = d/c.
Substitute: t = 600 km ÷ 300 000 km/s.
Result: t = 0.002 s (2 ms).
